$note: SC-001's oracle. This file DECLARES what the fixture corpus contains and which viewing key each transaction is relevant to; test/fixtures/shielded-monitor/build-corpus.ts SYNTHESIZES the matching bytes with the vendored ledger v8 WASM, and the tests compare the scanner's output against the `expected` fields here. The manifest is the authority: a test that recomputed the expectation from the same code that produced the bytes would prove nothing.
$why-not-committed-bytes: The transactions are built at test time rather than committed as blobs because the ledger's output ciphertexts carry fresh randomness on every construction (verified: two ZswapOffer.fromOutput calls over an identical CoinInfo serialize to different bytes). Committed bytes would therefore be one arbitrary sample presented as canonical, and a manifest keyed by their hashes would be unreproducible. The SHAPE is what is fixed here; the bytes are real ledger output built from it.
$seeds-are-test-only: `seed` values below are inputs to ZswapSecretKeys.fromSeed inside the test process. They are not keys, nothing derived from them is used on any network, and they must never be reused as real key material.

keys.role: the registered monitor's key: every positive is encrypted to it
the negative key: a second real wallet whose transactions must never match K
a third party, so a zero-match block contains a REAL transaction rather than nothing

one positive and one negative, side by side at two positions
a zero-match block that still advances coverage (US2 scenario 1)
multi-output, invisible-output, system, offer-less and (00009-07) input/transient-carrying transactions

Two wallets in one transaction: each must see only its own segment.
FR-008: several matching outputs in one transaction yield ONE association, not one per output.
Documented false-negative class: a contract-owned output carries no ciphertext for a user key, so NO viewing key can match it.
Never relevant, and never even deserialized: the scanner skips on `kind` (FR-006).

00009-07: the only corpus transaction carrying a real spent INPUT (a nullifier) and a real TRANSIENT (a commitment/nullifier pair) alongside two outputs to two different keys. Both the input and the transient are CONTRACT-owned, because the ledger refuses to build either from a user-owned output without the coin secret key (measured: 'attempted to spend a user-owned output as contract owned'), so neither can ever be `mine`. For K the guaranteed segment matches and two ciphertext-bearing outputs remain, which is the ambiguous attribution case: both read `mine: null` with `mineAmong: 2`.

The archivable stand-in for a reward-claim: a standard transaction carrying no zswap offer at all. Nothing can be encrypted to a key in it, so the predicate is vacuously false. (A real ClaimRewards transaction cannot be synthesized in archived form here -- see the fixture builder's own note.)
